reader_questions: Which scientific question is worth pursuing with the support available?
How can I develop an observation or analogy into a research idea?
What would distinguish competing explanations?
What can an inconclusive experiment establish?
C03.applicability: Scientific reasoning and design; this chapter does not prescribe a statistical analysis for every experiment.

reader_questions: How should I plan the next stage and decide whether to continue?
How can I keep up with relevant literature without reading everything?
What does this paper actually establish?
Can these studies be compared, and what do they establish together?
Which display makes the intended comparison visible?
How should observations, sampling units and uncertainty be shown?
How can color and symbols clarify a figure accessibly?
How do I assemble and check publication figures?
How should biological images be processed and presented without misleading comparisons?
What assumptions and encodings matter in specialized displays and diagrams?
What paper can the available evidence support?
How do the title, abstract and introduction explain the contribution?
How should methods, results and figure legends support reproducible interpretation?
How can I explain the meaning and limits of the findings?
How can I draft, assess and revise a complete paper?
Does this concern require clearer writing, new analysis or more evidence?
How can I organize a thesis around a coherent contribution?
C19.applicability: Thesis formats and permitted content depend on local requirements and supervisory expectations.

reader_questions: How much context does this audience need to understand the research?
How should I organize the explanation and slides for a talk?
How can I rehearse, deliver and answer questions about a talk?
How can a poster support both browsing and conversation?
How can I explain a project briefly or discuss a future program at a chalk talk?
How should I choose a journal and prepare a submission?
C25.applicability: Verify current journal instructions; cited policies are specific consulted examples.

reader_questions: How can I write a fair and useful manuscript review?
How should I revise a paper and respond to reviewers?
What should I do after rejection, a transfer offer or publication of reviews?
C28.applicability: Editorial procedures vary by journal and policy version.

reader_questions: Does this funding opportunity fit, and what will the application require?
How can a proposal connect significance, aims, experiments and feasibility?
How should I prepare for a funding interview and an award start?
C31.applicability: Selection does not by itself establish spending authority or access to resources.

reader_questions: Which kinds of scientific work fit my interests and constraints?
How can I assess an advisor and research environment?
How can my application materials demonstrate relevant contributions?
How should I find and apply for suitable positions?
How can I develop an independent program and evaluate a group-leader offer?
How can I manage a career transition and continuing responsibilities?
What support and independence does this researcher need?
Which shared expectations belong in a usable lab manual?
How can I lead a group within its actual capacity?
How can we diagnose and improve recurring working arrangements?
How should collaborators agree responsibilities, authorship and credit?
Which working arrangements support sustainable and fair participation?
How should I give feedback or respond to conflict?
